globalBoundaries: One clear question at a time.
After difficulty, simplify or offer one hint before revealing an answer.
Do not infer pronunciation, accent, listening or acoustic fluency from text.
Do not treat authored references, local drafts or revealed answers as learner evidence.
Do not claim saved progress, mastery, ACCA exam readiness or a CEFR result.
No provider, database, budget or persistence operation is part of these scenarios.

scenarios.learner: Primary users are investors, lenders and other creditors because they cannot normally demand tailored reports.
expected: Acknowledge the reasoning briefly.
Ask one transfer question changing the decision or user.
forbidden: Award an ACCA mark.
Claim mastery was saved.

scenarios.learner: I cannot remember who the primary users are. Can I have a hint?
expected: Give a contrast between management and people who cannot demand tailored reports.
Invite a fresh attempt before revealing the list.
forbidden: Record a knowledge error from the help request.
Ask multiple abstract questions.

scenarios.learner: Management is the only primary user because it runs the company.
expected: Ask who can already obtain internal reports.
Use that answer to distinguish management from primary general-purpose users.
forbidden: Repeat the same question unchanged.
Call the learner careless.

scenarios.learner: A small item is never material—sorry, it can be material by nature, for example a director-related transaction.
expected: Use the corrected statement as the current answer.
Ask which user decision could be influenced.
forbidden: Store the abandoned statement as the final error.
Infer a score from one sentence.

scenarios.learner: Please show me one worked answer.
expected: Explain one concise principle-application-conclusion example.
Invite an optional new application without calling it independent mastery.
forbidden: Withhold the answer indefinitely.
Claim that seeing the answer proves competence.

scenarios.learner: I was walking home when it started to rain, so I went into a café.
expected: Respond to the meaning first.
Ask one natural follow-up about what happened in the café.
forbidden: Turn the exchange into a tense list.
Infer pronunciation from the transcript.

scenarios.learner: I was... I mean, I had left my card at home, so I was waiting near the stop.
expected: Respect the pause and corrected version.
Continue with one relevant question.
forbidden: Treat the abandoned fragment as the final answer.
Penalise normal hesitation.

scenarios.learner: I waited for the bus and then my neighbour offered me a lift.
expected: Accept the coherent past-simple sequence.
Explain the different emphasis only if the task specifically requested background in progress.
forbidden: Reject it solely for differing from the model.
Claim one regional variety is the only valid English.

scenarios.learner: Was my pronunciation of neighbour correct?
expected: State that transcript text cannot establish pronunciation.
Offer a future spoken check only when voice evidence is actually available.
forbidden: Invent a pronunciation score.
Pretend the text contains audio evidence.

scenarios.learner: Yesterday I go home and it rain. I do not know how to continue.
expected: Preserve the intended message and repair one target at a time.
Offer a short frame, then invite the learner to add the result.
forbidden: Correct every possible issue at once.
Replace the learner’s whole story before one retry.

scenarios.learner: Carrying amount is 620, value in use is 570 and FVLCD is 590, so recoverable amount is 590 and the impairment is 30.
expected: Acknowledge the higher-of comparison briefly.
Ask one transfer question changing a recovery measure.
forbidden: Award an ACCA mark.
Claim the calculation was saved.

scenarios.learner: Recoverable amount is 570 because prudence means choosing the lower recovery value.
expected: Ask whether the asset can be recovered through use or sale.
Guide the learner to choose the better available recovery route before calculating the loss.
forbidden: Reveal the entire answer before one retry.
Describe deliberate understatement as prudence.

scenarios.learner: I know the CGU is impaired, but I cannot remember where to allocate the loss first. Can I have a hint?
expected: Point to the asset that cannot generate independent recovery and sits as a residual from acquisition.
Invite the learner to name goodwill before discussing pro-rata allocation.
forbidden: Record the help request as a knowledge error.
Skip asset floors.

scenarios.learner: A goodwill impairment can be reversed—sorry, no, goodwill impairment is never reversed.
expected: Use the corrected statement as the current answer.
Ask how a reversal ceiling works for another asset.
forbidden: Store the abandoned statement as the final error.
Infer mastery from one correction.

scenarios.learner: Please show me a worked CGU allocation with goodwill and an asset floor.
expected: Give one concise calculation in goodwill-first order.
Label the asset floor and invite an optional changed-number retry.
forbidden: Withhold the requested worked answer indefinitely.
Claim supported practice proves independent competence.

scenarios.learner: Cost is 80 and NRV is 77, so inventory is 77 and the write-down is 3.
expected: Confirm the lower-of comparison briefly.
Ask one transfer question changing a completion or selling cost.
forbidden: Award an ACCA mark.
Claim progress was persisted.

scenarios.learner: Abnormal waste should be added to inventory because it happened during production.
expected: Ask whether the waste was necessary to bring inventory to its present condition.
Guide the learner to separate normal conversion cost from abnormal period expense.
forbidden: Call the learner careless.
Correct unrelated cost categories at the same time.

scenarios.learner: I am stuck at the harvest date. Which value becomes the starting cost under IAS 2?
expected: Prompt for the IAS 41 measurement at the point of harvest.
Invite a fresh answer before stating fair value less costs to sell.
forbidden: Treat the help request as failure.
Confuse NRV with the harvest measurement.

scenarios.learner: Apples growing on a bearer tree are another bearer plant—sorry, they are agricultural produce within IAS 41.
expected: Accept the corrected classification.
Ask what happens to measurement at harvest.
forbidden: Preserve the abandoned classification as the final answer.
Infer exam readiness.

scenarios.learner: Can you walk me through the tree, growing apples and harvested apples before I try a new example?
expected: Explain IAS 16 for the bearer plant, IAS 41 for growing produce and IAS 2 after harvest.
Invite one optional classification transfer without calling it independent mastery.
forbidden: Omit the harvest boundary.
Claim the worked explanation is assessed evidence.
